title: An algebra through which every finitely presented algebra factors via a class E is a filtered colimit of members of E
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra, and $\mathcal E$ a set of commutative $R$-algebras each of finite presentation over $R$ (isomorphic as $R$-algebras to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ for some $n,m\ge0$). Assume: for every $R$-algebra $A$ of finite presentation and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ there are $B\in\mathcal E$ and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\beta:A\to B$, $\gamma:B\to\Lambda$ with $\gamma\circ\beta=\alpha$. Then $\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit of members of $\mathcal E$: there are a small filtered category $J$, a functor $j\mapsto B_j$ from $J$ to commutative $R$-algebras with $B_j\in\mathcal E$ for all $j$, and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\iota_j:B_j\to\Lambda$ such that $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_j)$ is a colimit of this diagram in the category of commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit, line 31952), proof of (2) implies (1): the full subcategory of the category of Lemma Tag 0BUF (lemma-ring-colimit-fp-category, line 31771: finitely presented R-algebras over Lambda, filtered with colimit Lambda) on the objects A -> Lambda with A in E is cofinal and filtered (Categories, Lemma Tag 0BUC, lemma-cofinal-in-filtered, categories.tex line 2230), so Lambda is its colimit (Categories, Lemma Tag 04E7, lemma-cofinal, line 1760); the converse direction (1) implies (2) is the node lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit

proof.text: *Step 1 (the category of finitely presented algebras over $\Lambda$).* Let $\mathcal P_0$ be the set of all $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I$ with $n\ge0$ and $I\subset R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ a finitely generated ideal, and $\mathcal P=\mathcal P_0\cup\mathcal E$. This is a set of $R$-algebras of finite presentation, and every $R$-algebra of finite presentation is isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal P_0\subset\mathcal P$ (by definition it is isomorphic to some $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$). Let $\mathcal I$ be the category of pairs $(A,\alpha)$, $A\in\mathcal P$, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, with morphisms $\varphi:(A,\alpha)\to(A',\alpha')$ the $R$-algebra maps $\varphi:A\to A'$ with $\alpha'\varphi=\alpha$, and let $D:\mathcal I\to$ (commutative $R$-algebras) be $(A,\alpha)\mapsto A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-colimit-fp-algebras-over-it], $\mathcal I$ is a small filtered category and $(\Lambda,(\alpha)_{(A,\alpha)\in\mathcal I})$ is a colimit of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit, line 31952), proof, second paragraph: 'Consider the category I of Lemma 0BUF'; Lemma Tag 0BUF (line 31771) and its footnote (objects restricted to a set)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the subcategory of members of $\mathcal E$, and the factorization).* Let $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal I$ be the full subcategory on the objects $(B,\beta)$ with $B\in\mathcal E$; it is small, as a full subcategory of the small category $\mathcal I$. Let $(A,\alpha)$ be an object of $\mathcal I$. Then $A$ is an $R$-algebra of finite presentation and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, so by the hypothesis there are $B\in\mathcal E$ and $R$-algebra maps $\beta:A\to B$, $\gamma:B\to\Lambda$ with $\gamma\circ\beta=\alpha$. Then $(B,\gamma)$ is an object of $\mathcal J$ (as $B\in\mathcal E\subset\mathcal P$) and $\beta$ is a morphism $(A,\alpha)\to(B,\gamma)$ of $\mathcal I$ (as $\gamma\beta=\alpha$). So every object of $\mathcal I$ has a morphism to an object of $\mathcal J$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C3 (lemma-when-colimit, line 31952), proof, second paragraph ('the full subcategory J consisting of those A -> Lambda with A in E'); hypothesis (2) of the lemma

proof.text: *Step 3 (cofinality, Categories 0BUC and 04E7).* The opposite category $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered, because the three conditions of filteredness of $\mathcal I$ (Step 1) are, read in $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$, the three conditions of cofilteredness; $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a full subcategory of $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$, and by Step 2 every object of $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ receives a morphism from an object of $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] to the cofiltered category $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$, its full subcategory $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$, the category of commutative $R$-algebras, and the functor $D:(\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathcal I\to$ (commutative $R$-algebras) of Step 1, whose colimit exists by Step 1. It gives: $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered, i.e. $\mathcal J$ is filtered (in particular nonempty); the restriction $D|_{\mathcal J}$ has a colimit $(L,(\lambda_{(B,\beta)})_{(B,\beta)\in\mathcal J})$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; and the canonical map $u:L\to\Lambda$, the unique $R$-algebra map with $u\circ\lambda_{(B,\beta)}=\beta$ for all $(B,\beta)\in\mathcal J$ (the coprojection of $D$ at $(B,\beta)$ being $\beta$ by Step 1), is an isomorphism.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 0BUC (lemma-cofinal-in-filtered, line 2230: J is filtered and cofinal in I) and Lemma Tag 04E7 (lemma-cofinal, line 1760: colim over J = colim over I), as cited in the proof of Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C3

proof.text: *Step 4 (conclusion).* Since $u$ is an isomorphism with $u\circ\lambda_{(B,\beta)}=\beta$, the cocone $(\Lambda,(\beta)_{(B,\beta)\in\mathcal J})$ is a colimit of $D|_{\mathcal J}$: for a cocone $(M,(\mu_{(B,\beta)}))$ on $D|_{\mathcal J}$ let $v:L\to M$ be the unique map with $v\lambda_{(B,\beta)}=\mu_{(B,\beta)}$; then $w=v u^{-1}$ satisfies $w\beta=v\lambda_{(B,\beta)}=\mu_{(B,\beta)}$, and any $w'$ with $w'\beta=\mu_{(B,\beta)}$ for all $(B,\beta)$ has $w'u\lambda_{(B,\beta)}=\mu_{(B,\beta)}$, so $w'u=v$ and $w'=w$. Thus $J:=\mathcal J$ is a small filtered category, $(B,\beta)\mapsto B_{(B,\beta)}:=B$ is a functor from $J$ to commutative $R$-algebras with every $B_{(B,\beta)}\in\mathcal E$, and the coprojections $\iota_{(B,\beta)}:=\beta$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras with $(\Lambda,(\iota_j)_{j\in J})$ a colimit of this diagram, which is the assertion.
